report: The 17-year-old male presents with oral and genital erosions, scattered vesicles, and a transient anosmia/ageusia prodrome. Repeatedly positive SARS-CoV-2 nucleic acid tests and negative Mycoplasma/other respiratory pathogen testing point to a viral mucocutaneous syndrome. The absence of culprit medication before onset makes drug-related hypersensitivity very unlikely. Autoimmune bullous disease remains less likely because skin biopsy DIF is pending. Thus the frontier is sufficiently refined: the most specific consensus hypothesis is COVID-19-associated mucocutaneous syndrome, supported by evidence and expert analyses.
